content.title: About
content.content: Pickled green beans are selected green bean pods that undergo a brining process with vinegar, spices, and salt. The beans retain a crisp texture and acquire a tangy‑sweet flavor. They are commonly used in salads, appetizers, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickled green beans are popular in Eastern European, Asian, and American cuisines.
Traditional brine includes vinegar, sugar, mustard seeds, dill, and black pepper.
The short pickling time helps preserve most B‑vitamins and minerals.
In Russia, pickled beans are a staple of holiday appetizer platters.
A sugar‑free “dry” brine version exists, making the product lower in calories.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Pickled beans contain little fat and few calories, suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Provides vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, iron, and magnesium, which aid immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermentation in the brine can generate beneficial bacteria that support gut health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in the beans help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salt level may be problematic for people with hypertension; consume in moderation.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Preservative additives
items.content: Commercial varieties may contain preservatives that can cause sensitivities.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic brine can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled green beans can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to salads, sandwiches, rice or noodle dishes, and used in cold appetizer platters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in a sealed jar. Properly stored, the beans stay crisp and flavorful for 3–4 weeks. Discard if mold appears or the smell changes.
